A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VLANeXt and contain readable text, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B. The original study and supplemental material can be matched reliably despite the added section and shifted numbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original LIBERO and LIBERO-plus experiments, real-world robot evaluations, and additional ablations and qualitative examples in Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds LIBERO evaluations of additional VLANeXt variants in Table 5.

M1.justification: Section 5 adds latent-action pretraining with VAE, VQ-VAE, and VICReg formulations; DINO latent-image prediction; and WAN2.2-based world-action models with fast and joint attention modes. It also describes additional action-training options. These substantially extend the available procedures while preserving the original VLANeXt recipe.

E1.justification: The represented datasets and tasks remain the four LIBERO suites, LIBERO-plus perturbations, DROID pretraining, and four real-world manipulation tasks. New variants are evaluated on retained LIBERO tasks; pooling existing suites for latent-action pretraining changes data use rather than coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 2–4 retain their comparator sets. New Table 5 substantially expands comparisons against original VLANeXt through evaluated VLANeXt-derived LAM, S/L/XL, JEPA, and fast/joint WAM baselines. Newly cited external WAM and JEPA systems are not themselves added as benchmark rows.

E3.justification: New LAM experiments introduce pretraining across all four LIBERO suites followed by labeled fine-tuning on each suite, unlike the retained direct per-suite fine-tuning setup. Table 5 also introduces additional backbone configurations. The explicit statement that LIBERO-plus uses no perturbation training clarifies the existing protocol rather than establishing a changed experiment.

E4.justification: Section 5 and Table 5 add analyses comparing latent-action regularizers, fast versus joint future-video attention, and DINO latent-image prediction, while extending backbone-scale analysis. These test several additional design questions. The original recipe ablations and appendix analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Reporting remains point success rates and real-world success/trial counts. v3 adds no training-seed or repeated-run information, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical tests; Table 5 follows the existing point-estimate practice.

E6.justification: Existing result tables and appendix ablations retain their values. New Table 5 adds nine variant rows: average success is 96.7 for S, 98.4 for L, 97.7 for XL and JEPA, and 98.2/97.6 for fast/joint WAM. LAM averages are 96.9, 96.8, and 97.6 for VICReg, VAE, and VQ-VAE. These are new configurations and training regimes, not revisions of earlier same-setting scores.

T1.justification: No new formal definitions, theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations are introduced. The added descriptions of latent-action constraints and training objectives are qualitative methodological explanations; the original mathematical content remains unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and original recipe claims remain, but the introduction and conclusion expand the contribution to a family of research baselines. They newly claim competitive compact models and complementary gains from larger backbones, latent-action pretraining, latent visual prediction, and world-action modeling.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly attributes the 8B model's shortfall to insufficient LIBERO data, latent-pretraining gains to additional cross-suite data, and JEPA gains to compact semantic DINO representations. These add interpretations without revising the original explanations or computational-cost caveats; the data-size explanation lacks a corresponding ablation.

D1.justification: v3 reports TFDS and LeRobot support, sequential/random episode loading, parallel evaluation rollouts, and EMA checkpoint saving. It also makes perturbation-free LIBERO training explicit. The code-access URLs and original detailed hyperparameter table, renumbered from Table 7 to Table 8, remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The extensions add contextual references including Latent-in-the-Wild, JEPA-VLA, FAST-WAM, Kairos, WAN, and language-action pretraining. They broaden connections to recent approaches while retaining Appendix B's related-work discussion and the core positioning as a controlled exploration of VLA design.

P1.justification: v3 extends the introduction and conclusion, inserts Section 5, and updates author affiliations. Most original prose and the appendix structure remain intact apart from cross-references and text reflow, so this is not an extensive rewrite or reorganization.

P2.justification: v3 adds a grouped, full-width Table 5 with backbone, loss, and per-suite result columns. Existing figures and tables undergo limited relocation, Table 3 gains a protocol clarification in its caption, and appendix tables are renumbered. The original figures and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Section 5 and Table 5 provide useful additional evidence about alternative VLANeXt designs while preserving the original study and appendices. The gain is limited by incomplete experimental details and absent uncertainty estimates. The broad latent-pretraining improvement claim also exceeds the results: only VQ-VAE averages above the original 97.4 baseline, at 97.6, with additional cross-suite pretraining data.
